messages:
maria: Anyone seen the generator stream goroutine get stuck if you cancel the ctx right after the first token? Repro'd this in the sampleapp and it leaks a goroutine.
kevin: Yup, ran into that yesterday. If you cancel the context immediately after Stream() starts, stream.Recv() never returns and the goroutine stays alive.
alex: Can you drop the tiny repro/snippet here?
maria: Sure — simplified version from sampleapps/gen-stream-demo:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
stream, err := client.Generator.Stream(ctx, req)
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
go func() { time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond); cancel() }()
for {
    chunk, err := stream.Recv()
    if err != nil { break }
    fmt.Println(chunk.Text)
}
```
On my machine the loop never exits; runtime.Stack shows a goroutine blocked in recv.
jake: That sounds like the recv path isn't watching ctx.Done. If the underlying read is blocked (network or pipe), cancel alone won't unblock it unless the transport is closed.
maria: Right — this is specific to generator streaming. Embeddings/call style stuff cancels fine. The generator uses an io.Pipe and the recv goroutine waits on the reader end. We probably need an explicit abort signal.
devex-bot: New issue created: #INF-342 StreamRecv blocked on ctx cancel — https://go.redwood/issue/INF-342
kevin: :thinking_face: Short-term workaround might be to call stream.Close() or expose an Abort method. Longer-term we should make Recv return on ctx cancellation.
nisha: Heads-up: the quickstart sample app for Go cancels contexts in a few places. If this stays unfixed, users following tutorials will hit this and see leaked goroutines. Marking high priority for DX.
alex: Agreed. We should either patch the SDK to observe ctx on Recv or add docs and change the sample app to not cancel until after stream finishes.
jake: My preference is to make Recv ctx-aware. I can prototype adding a select that returns when ctx.Done triggers and ensures the underlying transport is closed/aborted.
maria: I can add a failing unit/e2e test in sampleapps that reproduces the leak so CI catches regressions.
kevin: If we change Recv behavior, watch semver. Maybe gate behind an option like opts.WithInterruptibleStream(true) so we don't surprise users.
alex: :thumbsup: Also add an e2e to the nightly matrix. We should update onboarding docs if we can't land a fix this week.
devex-bot: Assigned to @jake, @kevin. ETA: EOW. Labels: ["go-sdk", "streaming", "p1"]
nisha: I'll take the doc/update for quickstarts if you all want me to.
maria: Thanks — pushed a tiny failing test to branch gen-stream-ctx-repro (https://go.redwood/pr/1234).
jake: I'll pick up that PR and iterate.
